_comment: Remote collector instances this machine may query, and the credential for each. Copy to remote_endpoints.json and fill in. The collector itself never reads this file - it does not know it exists. One program does: `python -m python.main watch`, the viewer, which takes the base_url and token of the entry named by --endpoint (default: live). For everything else it is a note to whoever is working here, machine-readable so a session does not have to be told the URL again.
_rules: The real file is gitignored. It never becomes tracked, never reaches the bus, never gets pasted into an issue.
One token per consumer, so revoking one does not disturb the others. This one is the operator's; the consuming project has its own; the viewer has its own.
The token authorises exactly the grants listed beside it. If a route answers 403, the grant is missing - it is not a bug in the route.
Print the URL freely, never the token. A command that needs it reads it from here.

live.instance_id: <minted at the data root on first start; /v1/status states it>
live.note: Which machine this reaches, and who maintains it

viewer.token: <40 characters, generated on the box, its own>
viewer.note: For `python -m python.main watch --endpoint viewer`. status:detail and nothing else: a viewer sits open on a desk all day, and a token that can also fetch archive files is a credential left lying in a window.

local.token: <the viewer token again, on the box itself>
local.note: The same viewer against a collector on this machine. Loopback, so it refreshes once a second instead of once every two.
